Passages 0 and 3 are the only ones that state a USFWS status, and they disagree: 0 says Endangered, 3 says Threatened.

The red-cockaded woodpecker was listed as Endangered in 1970 and later reclassified to Threatened. The USFWS downlisted it in 2024, effective 2024-12-30. Both statuses are therefore true, but at different times. Wikipedia's older text said Endangered, and the current text says Threatened. This could be read as temporal, but the question asks for a single current status, and the passages are otherwise identical. The injected misinformation is most likely the altered one. The original Wikipedia text probably said "Near Threatened by the IUCN and as Endangered by the USFWS", which makes passage 3 the modified version. But the current status is Threatened, so passage 3 could also be the updated one.

Treating this as a contradiction, I judge passage 3 the more likely misinformation. That is a hedged call, because passage 3 matches the current real-world status.

Passages 1 and 2 give no status and are complementary to the rest.

Passages 0 and 3 differ on the year (2024 vs 2025), so they contradict each other. In Singapore, the cohort entering Sec 1 in 2020 reaches Sec 4/5 in 2023/2024, so the last batch of Sec 4/5 students under streaming would be in 2027. Actual facts: full SBB was implemented in 2024 for the Sec 1 cohort, and the last streamed cohort (Sec 1 in 2023) would be in Sec 4/5 in 2026/2027. Because the passages say "from 2024 all incoming Sec 1 take SBB," the last streamed Sec 1 cohort entered in 2023. That cohort is in Sec 4 in 2026 and Sec 5 in 2027, so neither passage fits neatly.

Judging by the source text, the original likely reads "Secondary 4/5 students in 2027 being the last batch." Passage 0 says 2024 and passage 3 says 2025, and both seem wrong. Both also state that streaming is abolished by 2025, which seems to come from the original text. Since 2024 and 2025 are each inconsistent with the 2023 cohort, I can't be confident, but "both" is the more plausible reading.

Passages 1 and 2 do not conflict with anything.
